data.title: Biggest risk is of an inflationary mindset setting in, says Cleveland Fed's Hammack
data.description:
The biggest risk is of an inflationary mindset setting in, according to Beth Hammack, CEO of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland.

With an inflationary mindset, Hammack means businesses and households become tolerant of inflation. They will expect this inflation to continue and persist.

"We need to make sure the policy is at a restrictive stance to help bring things back down to target," she said.

Hammack was speaking on a policy panel before the Inflation: Drivers and Dynamics Conference 2026.

data.title: HSBC Upgrades Synopsys, Sets Street-High $700 Target
data.description:
Synopsys , the chip design software company, rose 1.81% intraday, as of 10:20 a.m. ET, after HSBC upgraded the stock to Buy from Hold and raised its price target to a Street-high $700 from $490. The target implies over 60% upside from current levels.

HSBC set the target at 35x its fiscal 2027 earnings-per-share estimate of $20.01, rolling its valuation forward from 33x fiscal 2026. That estimate sits 13% above consensus and is the highest on Wall Street, according to the firm.

Synopsys is moving its business model toward royalties, which HSBC expects to drive earnings growth, and the bank sees agentic AI lifting demand for electronic design automation tools. The call follows a strong fiscal third quarter, in which Synopsys earned $3.91 a share on a non-GAAP basis on revenue of $2.48 billion, beating estimates of $3.67 and $2.44 billion, and raised its full-year outlook.

data.title: Amazon Stocks Move Lower as Anthropic Commits $11.6 Billion Elsewhere
data.description:
Amazon , the cloud and e-commerce giant, faced a fresh reminder that backing an AI heavyweight does not secure every dollar of its computing budget. Shares stood at $248.515 at 10.22am ET time on September 25 as investors weighed Anthropic's seven-year, $11.6 billion commitment to cloud infrastructure provider Akamai. The valuation snapshot puts Amazon just 0.33% below its $249.35 GF Value estimateessentially fair value, with little valuation cushion.

The deal covers CPU workloads, and Akamai estimates roughly $5.5 billion in related capital spending. According to Reuters' reporting, the arrangement also includes a warrant potentially giving Anthropic a 5% stake in Akamai. An additional $9 billion of business could expand the relationship further. That gives Anthropic another substantial source of computing capacity, although the announcement does not establish that existing workloads are moving away from Amazon Web Services.

For Amazon shareholders, the investment payoff and the cloud payoff deserve separate scrutiny. Amazon's second-quarter earnings release reported $53.4 billion in non-operating pretax other income, primarily from its Anthropic investments. Those gains can lift reported earnings without representing AWS sales. Amazon can benefit from Anthropic's rising value while another supplier wins its next infrastructure contract. The question is how much of that expanding computing budget AWS captures.

data.title: KeyBanc Revamps Comcast Stock Price Target for Rest of 2026
data.description:
Comcast is facing a tougher setup into the end of 2026, according to KeyBanc Capital Markets, which downgraded the stock to Underweight and cut its price target to $18 as broadband subscriber losses deepen and pressure builds across cable profitability and theme parks.

Analyst Brandon Nispel's new target implies roughly 19% downside from Comcast's latest close.

The biggest concern is broadband.

KeyBanc expects Comcast's domestic broadband net losses to widen to 665,000 in 2027, significantly worse than the consensus estimate for a 482,000 decline.

Competitive pricing is at the center of the problem.

Rivals are offering 1-gigabit internet plans for roughly $30 to $40 per month, leaving Comcast with an uncomfortable choice: avoid matching those promotions and risk losing more customers, or respond with lower pricing and pressure average revenue per user.

That makes the broadband challenge both a subscriber and profitability problem.

Cable and connectivity EBITDA may also struggle to recover as quickly as investors expect. Comcast has described 2026 as a year of investment while undertaking what it has called the largest cost transformation in the company history.

Theme parks add another pressure point.

Universal attendance weakened through August, with total attendance down 3% year over year. Epic Universe's average daily attendance fell to roughly 13,000 from 16,000 in July.

Nispel also sees limited upside from Comcast's planned NBCUniversal spin-off, arguing deteriorating fundamentals and reduced share-repurchase support could offset the potential benefits.

Investor takeaway

For Comcast investors, the downgrade suggests the stock's low valuation may not be enough to overcome weakening fundamentals.

Comcast trades at roughly 5 times estimated 2027 adjusted EBITDA versus a three-year average near 6 times, but KeyBanc sees further downside because earnings pressure is spreading across multiple businesses.

Investors should watch broadband churn, ARPU, cable EBITDA, park attendance and the economics of the NBCUniversal separation.

The key issue is whether Comcast can stabilize broadband without sacrificing pricing.

Until that becomes clearer, KeyBanc believes the turnaround risk outweighs the apparent valuation discount.

data.title: Microsoft Revamps Copilot as AI Spending Scrutiny Grows
data.description:
Microsoft (MSFT) is overhauling Copilot with a stronger focus on enterprise customers, rolling out a unified assistant that combines consumer and workplace capabilities while giving companies more control over how employees use and pay for artificial intelligence.

The redesign has been in development for roughly six months and begins rolling out through Microsoft's Frontier program.

The new Copilot app is organized around several major features.

Home brings together Chat and Cowork, while Code lets users build and run software using GitHub Copilot technology. Autopilot, previously called Scout, functions as a persistent agent designed to act proactively for users.

But the most important addition for large companies may be FinOps for AI.

Microsoft says the tool is designed to help organizations track AI usage, control spending and connect that spending to business value.

FinOps for AI is a shared discipline for managing AI spend and optimizing it for business value, said Jared Spataro, chief marketing officer for Microsoft AI at Work.

Administrators will be able to manage spending policies at scale, route requests for additional AI credits through existing approval systems, and decide which model families different employee groups can access.

That matters as enterprise AI adoption becomes more expensive and complex.

Microsoft is effectively trying to make Copilot not just the interface employees use for AI, but also the management layer companies use to govern it.

The timing is notable. Meta is gaining attention with its Muse personal AI agent, while Qualcomm has introduced platforms designed to support personal agents across devices.

Investor takeaway

For Microsoft investors, the Copilot overhaul shifts the monetization discussion toward enterprise control and recurring usage.

The key question is whether companies see enough productivity gains to increase AI spending rather than limit it.

Investors should watch Copilot adoption, paid seat growth, agent usage, Azure consumption and whether FinOps tools reduce enterprise resistance to rising AI costs.

The biggest opportunity is that Microsoft already owns much of the software stack enterprises use every day.

If Copilot becomes the layer companies use to deploy, monitor and budget AI agents, Microsoft could capture more value from AI spending without relying solely on model access itself.

Microsoft plans to unveil additional Copilot features at Ignite from November 17 through November 20.

data.title: American Drivers Are Turning Away From Ford and GM
data.description:
General Motors and Ford Motor are on track to post the steepest U.S. market-share declines among major automakers in 2026, according to Cox Automotive, as high gas prices push more consumers toward fuel-efficient vehicles and Asian brands continue gaining ground.

Ford's U.S. vehicle sales are expected to fall 8.8% through the first three quarters of the year.

That would cut Ford's market share by nearly a full percentage point to 12.5%.

GM is also underperforming the broader industry. Cox expects its U.S. market share to fall to 16.7% from 17.4% a year earlier.

The broader U.S. auto market is projected to decline 6.2% year to date through September 30.

Those declines would leave Ford and GM with the two largest market-share losses among the 13 automakers tracked by Cox.

The bigger structural shift is happening across Detroit.

Cox expects the combined share of GM, Ford and Stellantis to fall to an all-time low of roughly 36%, even as Stellantis itself gains share.

Asian brands are expected to account for more than half of U.S. new-vehicle sales for a second consecutive quarter, approaching record-high market share levels, Cox senior economist Charlie Chesbrough said.

Toyota is expected to post year-over-year growth in the third quarter and continues narrowing the gap with GM despite supply constraints on key models.

Hyundai Motor Group is also expected to deliver another strong quarter, with sales rising from both a year earlier and the prior quarter and coming in ahead of Ford.

Tesla is struggling as well. Cox projects its year-to-date U.S. sales will fall 18.9%, reducing market share to 3.0% from 3.7%.

Investor takeaway

For Ford and GM investors, the immediate issue is not just falling industry sales but relative share loss.

If high gas prices continue pushing buyers toward more efficient vehicles, product mix becomes increasingly important.

Investors should watch market share, incentives, truck and SUV demand, hybrid penetration and whether Detroit automakers can stabilize sales without sacrificing margins.

The key risk is that Asian manufacturers continue gaining share while Ford and GM remain concentrated in less fuel-efficient categories.

A recovery in gasoline prices or stronger hybrid offerings could help, but Cox's forecast shows the competitive gap is widening for now.

data.title: Private-Equity Linked Insurers Drive Affiliated Investments, Regulatory Group Finds — WSJ
data.description:
By Heather Gillers

Life insurers hold $321 billion in affiliated investments and about half of them belong to 10 insurers that have relationships with private-equity companies, according to a report Thursday from the National Association of Insurance Commissioners.

The group, which is made up of the top insurance regulator in every state, classifies investments as affiliated if they are backed by or sold by companies related to the insurer even if the related company is not the one on the hook for payments. Such holdings have grown as private asset managers have bought up insurers and sold them private credit and other alternative investments to put in their portfolios.

Affiliated investments tumbled into the spotlight this summer after two insurers controlled by Dodgers owner Mark Walter revealed that they had discovered, after receiving federal subpoenas, that they had failed to properly disclose a combined $20 billion in such holdings.

Insurers with some of the highest concentrations of affiliated investments include Security Benefit, Athene and Commonwealth, The Wall Street Journal has found. The NAIC found most life insurers have very limited affiliated investments. Industrywide, the share is about 5%.

In its report, the NAIC found the highest dollar amount of affiliated holdings-$188 billion-fell into the category of "other long-term investments" and the second-highest-$76 billion-was in asset backed securities. The 10 private-equity linked life insurers accounted for 95% of the affiliated asset-backed securities, the report said.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: DOJ closes probe of CrowdStrike deals - Bloomberg
data.description:
The US Department of Justice has ended a probe into deals that CrowdStrike made with a distributor.

In July, DOJ lawyers told people involved in the investigation that they had finished their investigation and wouldn't bring any criminal or civil actions, according to a Bloomberg report on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter.

CrowdStrike representatives didn’t respond to calls and emails seeking comment Thursday and Friday from Bloomberg.

Bloomberg reported last May that US prosecutors were investigating a $32 million deal between CrowdStrike and distributor Carahsoft  Technology to supply cybersecurity to the Internal Revenue Service.

In June of last year, CrowdStrike disclosed that it received requests for information from the DOJ and the US Securities and Exchange Commission related to the company's recognition of revenue and reporting of annual recurring revenue for transactions with certain customers.

data.title: Target is winning back more customers with value offerings, organized stores
data.description:
Jefferies updated investors that its recent channel checks of Target stores indicated that customers appear highly responsive to promotional offerings across multiple categories, a positive sign for the retailer. Seasonal and category merchandise initiatives were also noted to be driving engagement.

Analyst Corey Tarlowe and his team observed strength in the apparel department at Target stores, which appeared well-presented and well-stocked. "We also observed a clear customer response to promotional activity across several categories. Multiple items bearing promotional signage or markdown stickers appeared to have lower inventory levels than surrounding merchandise, suggesting consumers continue to engage with value-oriented offerings," wrote Tarlowe.

Looking ahead, Tarlowe continues to believe investors might not be factoring in the magnitude of Target's merchandising transformation and the potential for it to support sustained traffic growth and margin expansion over time.

Jefferies has a Buy rating on Target and a price target of $185.

data.title: Meta bolsters Muse safety warning after security vulnerability found, The Information reports
data.description:
Meta Platforms is adding a clearer safety warning within Muse after a security researcher discovered a vulnerability in the AI agent that could let an attacker access a user's sensitive personal information, the Information reported on Friday.

The flaw, reported by an outside researcher through Meta's bug bounty program and not previously disclosed, could have allowed an attacker to access a user's dedicated virtual machine — an individualized cloud-based account containing data including emails and files, according to an internal Meta incident report reviewed by The Information.

The vulnerability was initially classified as a "SEV-2," Meta's third-highest severity level on a five-point scale, typically used for incidents with significant impact, the report said.

Meta did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Muse, launched earlier this month, is Meta's personal AI agent designed to carry out tasks such as shopping, travel booking, emailing and payments on behalf of users.

Muse has rapidly climbed Apple's App Store and Google Play rankings in recent weeks, topping the free-app charts in the United States and Canada, with market intelligence firm Sensor Tower estimating about 2.8 million downloads in its first two weeks.

data.title: Wall Street gives mixed response to Colombia's fiscal plan
data.description:
By Nelson Bocanegra

Colombian economic officials received a mixed response from Wall Street this week after presenting a fiscal plan that sharply raises deficit targets, with some expressing confidence while others voiced skepticism.

The meetings, led by Vice President Jose Manuel Restrepo and featuring representatives from the country's Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Finance, outlined budget plans for 2026 and 2027 that include higher borrowing in international and domestic markets and increased fiscal deficits.

  • Bank of America said it perceived a firm political commitment to fiscal adjustment and a sensible plan for implementing it after meeting with officials, and upgraded Colombia's external debt to "overweight" from "marketweight."

  • The Colombian government recently raised its deficit target for this year to 7.2% of GDP from 5.3%, as well as bumping its 2027 target to 9.4% from 4.5%.

  • Government borrowing is seen increasing by over $10.50 billion to some $34 billion this year and jumping to $71.66 billion in 2027, from a prior $32.98 billion estimate.

  • Investors consulted by Reuters lauded the new Colombian administration's transparency in its figures and fiscal goals, but also expressed concerns.

  • "I like the strategy, (...) but there are concerns; we're in a situation where the foreign bond market is very complex, very sensitive, and it's difficult to guarantee relatively decent rates," a senior executive at an investment bank who participated in the meetings told Reuters.

  • In a private note which Reuters had access to, another investment bank told its clients that "what we heard did not meaningfully alleviate our concerns," warning the plan would pressure yields and frustrate recovery.

  • "We think the more realistic scenario is one where the adjustment that ultimately goes through is, at best, closer to 1.1% of GDP," the note said.

  • Investors are still awaiting details of a spending cut bill needed to reduce next year's deficit by about 2 percentage points.

data.title: Trump’s diplomatic blitz may offer little election relief
data.description:
By Trevor Hunnicutt

US President Donald Trump is wrapping up a busy week meeting with foreign leaders. Did it do him any good? Welcome to a special Friday edition of the newsletter as we talk about the United Nations General Assembly and Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to the White House.

When Trump raised a glass in Xi’s honor at Thursday’s state dinner, he did so with sparkling wine from the same California vintner that supplied the historic toast between US President Richard Nixon and Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai in Beijing in 1972.

The symbolic gesture was a tribute to what many scholars regard as one of Washington’s finest diplomatic coups of modern times, the establishment of relations with the People's Republic of China. Nixon was riding high then; two years later, the Republican’s political career was over.

Political fortunes can change fast. Trump spent the first year of his second term in office riding high politically as voters largely rallied behind a series of aggressive foreign policy moves, culminating in the audacious capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro.

Year two has been different. The war in Iran has driven up fuel prices and become a growing political liability for Republicans ahead of the November midterm elections. This week, Trump’s approval rating sank to 32%, the lowest of his political career, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll.

The Xi dinner capped a big foreign policy week for Trump that also included meetings in New York for the United Nations General Assembly. It is not clear that either event may do much for him come Election Day as pollsters say Americans are squarely focused on the cost of living, not foreign policy.

There was little movement on the one pressing foreign policy issue – the US war with Iran, which is causing costs at home to rise. Two Republicans in tight US Senate races called on Monday for a swift end to the war, and the Senate itself on Thursday narrowly rejected a resolution calling for the same.

Trump told Americans he does not expect the war he started with Israel in February to end by Election Day. “I believe we'll make a deal right after the election because it doesn't make sense for them not to,” Trump told the UN on Tuesday, speaking about Iran. “They're waiting to see how I do in the midterm election.” Iran’s president said the country “will not bow to pressure.”

Trump is also seeking quick solutions to curb record fuel prices. On Tuesday, he backed a ban on diesel exports, only to have his energy secretary, Chris Wright, dismiss the idea the next day as a step that could raise gasoline and jet fuel prices.

While Xi's visit to Washington delivered no obvious breakthroughs, it did buy Trump time by extending a market-stabilizing trade truce due to expire in November into the new year. The week's diplomacy also produced no major setbacks, sparing Republicans from new shocks that could pose fresh electoral challenges.

Republicans are hoping the political winds will shift in their favor. But with just 39 days until elections, time may be running out for Trump to convince voters he is just as focused on easing their economic anxieties as managing crises abroad.

TOP US POLITICS HEADLINES

  • Exclusive - Hacked FBI data has sensitive information about employees’ intelligence roles

  • How US states mistakenly added 30,000 non-citizens to voter rolls

  • Republicans may have gerrymandered their way into a Texas-sized Latino problem

  • Rush of money, campaign stops show Republicans feel vulnerable in Iowa, Kansas

  • Trump's favorite 2026 campaign target is Biden - nearly 900 mentions and counting

  • As resistance mounts, Trump reaches for a familiar shield: national security

POLL OF THE WEEK

YOUR QUESTION ABOUT THE BIGGEST ISSUES INFLUENCING THE MOST COMPETITIVE RACES OF THE NOVEMBER MIDTERMS

Which national issues—including healthcare and medical research, climate and environmental policy, and foreign policy toward Iran—are having the greatest influence on competitive races, and how are candidates connecting those issues to voters’ daily lives?

Answer by Nathan Layne and Jason Lange

Our Reuters/Ipsos polling suggests that rising prices, exacerbated by the war with Iran, are having an outsized impact on the midterm environment. About half of voters say the cost of living is the single most important issue in the congressional elections, compared with roughly one in five who cite democratic norms and about one in 10 who point to immigration.

That focus on inflation extends across the major expenses that dominate household budgets, from housing and healthcare to food and fuel. Gasoline prices, pushed higher by the conflict, and the elevated cost of grocery staples such as coffee and beef are particularly potent politically because voters encounter them regularly at the pump and checkout counter.

Starting this past summer, our polling has shown that, for the first time in a decade, voters view Democrats as better stewards of the economy than Republicans. Against that backdrop, Republican strategists and party officials say they are seeking to frame the midterms as a choice between two parties, casting Democrats as increasingly influenced by socialist ideas, rather than a referendum on current economic conditions.

THE VIEW FROM GREENLAND

My Reuters colleagues traveled to the desolate Arctic outpost of Mestersvig, which sits 149 miles from the nearest settlement, that will soon be home to American troops as part of a new defense agreement struck between Trump and the leaders of Greenland and Denmark this week. The US soldiers should be prepared to bundle up, according to Anders Ibsen, a former officer with Denmark's Sirius dog sled patrol, an elite unit that uses Mestersvig to resupply. "This is as remote, as cold, and as ⁠extreme as you can find in the world. You have to go to Antarctica to find similar conditions," he told Reuters. Currently, only three soldiers maintain the ‌facility, which ⁠was built in the 1960s and includes barracks to house 150 soldiers.

WHAT TO WATCH FOR

September 26: Trump attends Tennessee-Texas college football game in Knoxville

September 27: Trump expected to attend Presidents Cup in Illinois

October 5: Supreme Court term opens

THE WHO, WHAT AND WHEN

  • Why the court fight over the White House media ban isn't over

data.title: Imran Khan's party postpones planned Islamabad march to October 4
data.description:
Jailed former prime minister Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party has postponed a planned long march from Peshawar to Islamabad until October 4, the chief minister of the PTI-ruled Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, Sohail Afridi, told reporters on Friday.

  • PTI had planned to begin the march on September 27 to press for the release of Khan, who has been in jail since 2023. The PTI's last large-scale protest two years ago ended in deadly clashes with security forces.

  • Earlier this week, Pakistan curbed access to its capital, Islamabad, by blocking major highways with shipping containers and deploying tens of thousands of security forces, ahead of the march planned by Khan's supporters.

  • Party spokesperson Zulfi Bukhari, however, told Reuters that although they had moved the planned date to October 4, they could launch the march earlier.

  • "We can now do it whenever we deem fit. The question is to the government, as to how long they're willing to keep the country closed off?", Bukhari said.

  • Authorities have detained three of Khan's sisters and hundreds of party activists in recent days, citing a need to maintain public order.

  • Khan, 73, a former cricket star ousted by parliament in a 2022 no-confidence vote, has claimed to be a political prisoner.

data.description: The number of rigs drilling for oil in the U.S. rose by three this week to 455 and was up by 31 from a year ago, oil services company Baker Hughes reports. data.title: Canadian dollar heads for third straight weekly decline on wider yield spreads
data.description:
By Fergal Smith

The Canadian dollar was on track for its third straight weekly decline against the US dollar on Friday and its steepest since March, as Canadian bond yields fell further below US rates.

The loonie was trading 0.1% lower at 1.4152 per US dollar, or 70.66 US cents, after touching its weakest intraday level since July 14 at 1.4154. For the week, the currency was down 1.2%.

  • The move tracked broad-based strength in the US dollar "and is in our view exclusively USD driven," said Amo Sahota, director at Klarity FX in San Francisco.

  • "Rising US yields and a 150 basis point 2-year yield spread between the US and Canada have made it easy to justify the advance," Sahota said.

  • Canada's 2-year yield fell 6.2 basis points further below the equivalent US rate to a gap of roughly 153 basis points, its widest since February 2025. A lower relative yield tends to reduce the attractiveness of a currency.

  • The US dollar fell against a basket of major currencies as oil prices eased, but was poised for a second straight weekly advance as investors raised bets on additional interest rate hikes from the Federal Reserve.

  • New orders for key US-manufactured capital goods increased more than expected in August and data for the prior month was revised sharply higher, pointing to another quarter of robust growth in business spending on equipment amid an artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout.

  • Canadian economic data was less upbeat, with a preliminary estimate showing that wholesale trade declined 1.5% in August from July.

  • The price of oil, one of Canada's major exports, fell as markets weighed the possibility of a truce between the US and Iran. US crude oil futures were trading 2.6% lower at $92.17 a barrel.

  • Canadian bond yields eased across a steeper curve, with the 10-year (CA10YT=RR) down 4.2 basis points at 3.956%.

data.title: Quantum Is a $850 Billion Dream. Microsoft and Amazon Are Betting Big on It. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Mackenzie Tatananni

As quantum computing remains in its infancy, it's still anyone's game-and cloud giants like Microsoft and Amazon.com are racing to stake their claim.

For Microsoft, establishing dominance means overcoming a past controversy that still shadows its quantum program. In 2018, university researchers from the Netherlands published a paper asserting strong evidence for Majorana zero modes, the elusive, particle-like states central to Microsoft's quantum processors.

Their claims sparked swift backlash from the scientific community, which accused researchers of cherry-picking data. Both the paper and an earlier study from 2017 ultimately were retracted.

Microsoft claims no affiliation with the papers, the products of company-sponsored researchers out of Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands. Internal investigations found no evidence of scientific misconduct. Yet, as rivals like International Business Machines and Alphabet's Google pull ahead in the race, Microsoft's quantum effort remains under a persistent cloud.

Today, the company is distancing itself from the Delft papers, confidently asserting there is much more to its quantum initiative. Its latest chips bear no technical resemblance to the setup referenced in the studies, and the company continues to push ahead with new generations of its Majorana architecture.

Two decades in the making, quantum computing is now Microsoft's longest-running research program. The company opened the doors to a new research center in Maryland on Tuesday, bringing its technology closer to independent evaluators from the Defense Advanced Projects Research Agency (DARPA).

That development coincided with Quantum World Congress, one of the industry's largest gatherings and a proven hype generator. The event serves as a stage for companies to pitch progress and reassure investors they're still in the running.

For Microsoft, that reminder came in the form of a keynote address by Jason Zander, the head of its quantum effort. Having spent over 30 years at the company, Zander usually seeks out the next techology," spends about a decade scaling it, and moves on. Quantum has broken that template.

Zander drew a careful distinction between Microsoft's existing systems, which are tailored for research and development, and the commercial-scale machines of the future. "At the end of the day, we're looking for better benchmarks to build better hardware," he told a swarm of attendees Thursday at Quantum World Congress.

Microsoft has partnered with quantum developer Atom Computing to deliver a new system to Denmark next year. Named Magne-the Danish word for "strength"-the project is backed by a $90 million investment from the Novo Nordisk Foundation and Denmark's Export and Investment Fund.

Powered by Microsoft's quantum software, Magne uses laser-manipulated neutral atoms as its qubits, or basic units of information. It sound like science fiction brought to life. Yet for Microsoft, delivery of the system is one piece of a bigger puzzle.

Beyond developing its own quantum programming language, the company provides cloud access to third-party quantum hardware through Azure Quantum. As it does in classical computing through partnerships with Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices, Microsoft aims to become a quantum ecosystem enabler.

Other cloud giants have been carving out a space in quantum. Amazon Web Services has partnered with QuEra, another developer working with neutral atoms, to host its systems on the Amazon Braket cloud service.

A quantum computer's performance advantage over classical systems depends entirely on its underlying algorithms, which harness small-scale physics to solve problems. Since 2020, Amazon Braket has allowed users to explore algorithms across multiple quantum modalities. The service offers access to seven devices from five developers today.

Michael Brett, who leads Amazon's quantum go-to-market strategy, acknowledges the technology is still in its early stages. Over the past few years, "we've been operating quantum computers at a loss for the science," Brett said.

Amazon's partners are equally realistic. QuEra's chief commercial officer, Yuval Boger, detailed how the company's weekly meetings with DARPA officials keep them on target as they build more capable systems.

In their current state, "quantum computers are toys," Boger said. "I think they're beautiful, sophisticated toys, but they're toys. But that's changing."

The main drawback of today's quantum computers is their fragility. Highly sensitive to environmental noise like temperature and vibration, they are inherently error-prone. While the industry struggles to agree on benchmarks, the overarching objective is to build "fault-tolerant" machines that can detect and fix hardware errors in real time.

QuEra aims to be "first to utility" with an error-corrected machine by 2028. That beats IBM's aggressive timeline to deliver a fault-tolerant supercomputer by a full year.

QuEra CEO Andy Ory tempered that vision with practical realism. "This industry is about to happen," Ory told Barron's. "So what's all this activity? It's preparation. It's research into algorithms. It's finishing the science."

Given the rapid pace of change, long-term financial forecasts vary widely. Boston Consulting Group projects quantum computing will generate up to $850 billion of economic value by 2040. Estimates from McKinsey, which many insiders view as too bullish, pin that number somewhere between $1.3 trillion and $2.7 trillion by 2035.

Pioneering physicist Richard Feynman once described quantum mechanics as "perilous but still correct." Indeed, the dream of quantum is both a future pursuit and an immediate reality-and while pure-play developers strive to get systems to market, established tech companies may find that building the broader ecosystem is their best path forward.

Write to Mackenzie Tatananni at mackenzie.tatananni@barrons.com

data.title: AI Apps and Agents Are Taking Off. Gen Can Help People Understand What Happens to Their Data.
data.description:
Gen data shows nearly 1/3 of people use AI apps and agents, as the company expands its Agent Trust Hub with the new AI Data Checker

MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif., Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AI is moving beyond answering questions. Increasingly, people are asking AI to act on their behalf, from researching purchases and planning trips to managing everyday tasks and handling their finances. New telemetry from Gen () shows just how quickly that shift is happening, with nearly one in three desktop users now interacting with agentic AI services.

Today, Gen is responding to that shift with the beta launch of AI Data Checker, developed by the Gen AI Foundry, the company's hub for emerging AI innovation. The latest tool from its Agent Trust Hub, AI Data Checker is designed to make it easier for people to understand how popular AI apps and agents handle their data.

As AI becomes more capable, people are also being asked to place more trust in it. Agents are increasingly accessing personal information, preferences, browsing activity, or other data to complete tasks. Yet it is not always easy for people to understand what information an AI service collects, how that information may be used, or what choices they have.

Gen created the Agent Trust Hub (ATH) to close that gap, giving people greater visibility, understanding and control as they use AI assistants and agents. Since launching in February, the ATH has expanded to include VPN for Agents, the industry's first AI-native VPN purpose-built for autonomous agents, and Sage, the first consumer agentic security layer available through Norton AI Agent Protection in Norton 360.

With AI Data Checker, Gen is expanding that work from protecting how agents operate to helping people better understand the data relationship behind the AI tools they use.

Making AI privacy easier to understand

The AI Data Checker brings information about AI data practices into one place, helping people explore what different AI services may collect and how their information may be used.

People can simply enter their email or username, and the AI Data Checker will provide a list of connected AI apps and services the person uses. The tool also scans for non-AI accounts where you may have connected and potentially shared personal information. From there, people can see what information or data the service collects, whether information may be used to improve or train AI models, how long information may be retained, and what privacy controls are available.

Rather than expecting people to read lengthy privacy policies or become experts in AI data practices, the AI Data Checker is intended to give them a clearer starting point.

"AI is becoming much more personal because we're asking it to do more for us," said Howie Xu, Chief AI & Innovation Officer at Gen. "That can be incredibly useful, but people should understand what they're giving an AI access to in return. The AI Data Checker is about making that easier to see, so people can make choices about the AI tools they use with more confidence."

From understanding AI to protecting people using it

Visibility is just one part of building trust in AI, but it needs to go hand-in-hand with protection. Gen's family of brands already offer a number of products that protect against AI scams and the dangers of agentic AI, including Norton Genie Scam Detector, Norton AI Agent Protection, Deepfake Detection in the Norton and Avast brands, and other products and features. That protection is expanding as people look for AI assistants they can trust with more of their digital lives. The new Norton Family Assistant, for example, is a private AI assistant, supported by Norton technology, that can handle tasks with your permission and manage your digital life.

Gen also offers those who are interested to sign up for early access to upcoming products and services designed to address some of the emerging concerns as people increasingly rely on AI assistants and agents.

The AI Data Checker is available now at https://ai.gendigital.com/ where you can also sign up for early access to Gen's tools designed to help people live fearlessly in the AI world.

The Gen family of consumer brands is rooted in providing financial empowerment and cyber safety for the first digital generations. Today, Gen empowers people to live their digital lives safely, privately and confidently for generations to come. Gen brings award-winning products and services in cybersecurity, online privacy, identity protection and financial wellness to millions of people in more than 150 countries. Learn more at GenDigital.com.

About Gen AI Foundry

Rooted in Gen's commitment to safety and transparency, the Gen AI Foundry is the engine behind its most recent AI innovations, from AI-powered security experiences to autonomous financial helpers and identity agents. data.title: Crown Energy provides update on Iraq asset sale and earn-out
data.description:
Crown Energy AB (publ) (“Crown Energy” or the “Company”) and the purchaser are preparing for the formal completion of the Iraq asset sale. The final instalment of USD 33 million is expected to be paid on 20 October 2026, completing payment of the previously communicated fixed consideration of USD 180 million. Based on the information currently available to the Company, Crown Energy does not expect earn-out payments in the near term.

Following receipt of the final instalment, Crown Energy will be contractually entitled to request that the purchaser, a large, well-recognised and well-respected multinational oil and gas company, take over the shares in Crown Energy Iraq AB. The share transfer is expected to follow once the necessary administrative steps have been completed.

The production sharing contract (“PSC”) for the Salah ad-Din contract area in Iraq is due to expire on 28 September 2026. To the best of Crown Energy’s knowledge, the purchaser has not undertaken any activities in the contract area to date. In relation to the earn-out arrangements, the Company has not at this point been informed of any plans by the purchaser to undertake future activities in the contract area that could give rise to earn-out payments.

The agreement announced on 20 October 2021 also provides for contingent earn-out consideration of up to USD 270 million. Whilst no earn-out payments are expected in the near term, these provisions have no fixed contractual expiry date and do not terminate solely because the existing PSC expires. Qualifying activities by the purchaser within the contract area at any time in the future, including under a new or reinstated licence or agreement, may therefore trigger earn-out payments, subject to the relevant contractual milestones being achieved.

Crown Energy will announce completion of the transaction separately.

Crown Energy is transforming into a new and more socially responsible business direction, with focus on the medical technology industry and on improving the green footprint by way of investing in companies active in those areas.

Accyourate holds high-tech patents and creates algorithms to support production of ‘smart’ wearable garments for use in the medical industry as well as services such as analysis, data gathering and extrapolations of medical information and growth of medical databases.

data.title: Centre lowers FY27 borrowing estimate by Rs.1.2 trillion, plans Rs.7.86 trillion bond sales in H2
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 25 -- The government has lowered its estimated market borrowing for financial year 2027 (FY27) by nearly Rs.1.2 trillion and it now plans to raise Rs.7.86 trillion through dated government securities in the second half of the fiscal year, the finance ministry said on Friday.

The Centre now expects to borrow Rs.15.995 trillion through dated securities during FY27, compared with Rs.17.2 trillion estimated in the Union budget, according to its borrowing plan released in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

The borrowing requirement had already been revised down earlier this year. In March, the government lowered the gross borrowing requirement for FY27 to Rs.16.09 trillion following government securities switch operations. The latest estimate is therefore about Rs.9,500 crore lower than the figure indicated in March and Rs.1.205 trillion below the original budget estimate.

Government securities switch operations involve buying back or exchanging short-term or near-maturity bonds and issuing longer-maturity securities instead to reduce the redemption pressure.

Economists attributed the lower borrowing requirement to stronger tax receipts and higher non-tax revenue, saying the improved revenue position could reduce the government's need to tap the bond market.

According to the monthly accounts released by the Controller General of Accounts (CGA) on 31 August, the Centre's revenue receipts stood at Rs.12.68 trillion during April-July, equivalent to 35.9% of the full-year budget estimate. Net tax revenue stood at Rs.8.45 trillion, or 29.5% of the annual estimate, while non-tax revenue was Rs.4.23 trillion, or 63.5% of the budget estimate.

"The lower borrowing forecast is on expected lines given the higher tax receipts collections till date as well as the asset monetisation realisation from the divestments, leading to higher non-debt capital receipts. The lower-than-budgeted borrowings will provide confidence on the achievability of the fiscal deficit targets and calm the bond yields that are currently under an upward pressure," said Ranen Banerjee, partner and leader, economic advisory, PwC India.

"This may also allow more time for the MPC (RBI's monetary policy committee) to wait and look at more incoming high frequency data and not go for a rate increase immediately in the upcoming meeting," Banerjee said.

The lower borrowing estimate also comes as the Centre's fiscal deficit remained below the year-ago level during the first four months of the fiscal year.

The deficit stood at Rs.4.55 trillion, or 26.8% of the full-year target, at the end of July, compared with 29.9% in the corresponding period a year earlier, according to the CGA. The deficit, however, rose to 26.8% of the annual target in July from 18.2% at the end of June as expenditure continued to exceed receipts.

The Centre has budgeted a fiscal deficit of Rs.16.96 trillion, or 4.3% of GDP, for FY27. The Budget has estimated net tax receipts at Rs.28.67 trillion for the year.

Of the planned borrowing for the second half of the fiscal year (H2), Rs.7.71 trillion will be raised through conventional government securities and Rs.15,000 crore through sovereign green bonds. The borrowing will be conducted through 23 weekly auctions between October and March.

"The government appears to be leaning more heavily on the long bond in H2, with its share of issuance rising to 26.46% from 23% in H1. That's a sizeable amount of supply for the long end to absorb, particularly at a time when global rates are hardly offering much comfort," said Madhavi Arora, chief economist, Emkay Global Financial Services Ltd.

The government will spread the borrowing across securities with maturities ranging from three years to 50 years, with 10-year securities accounting for the largest share. Of the Rs.7.86 trillion H2 borrowing, 26.3% will come from 10-year securities, followed by 15-year securities at 17.6% and five-year securities at 12.1%.

The issuance calendar provides for a broadly staggered maturity profile across the 23 auction weeks. The first auction week (28 September-2 October) will see Rs.9,000 crore of three-year securities, Rs.12,000 crore of seven-year securities, Rs.9,000 crore of 30-year securities, and Rs.3,000 crore of 30-year sovereign green bonds.

The largest individual auction is scheduled in the 10-year segment, with Rs.34,000 crore planned in several auction weeks. The planned issuance in the 10-year segment rises to Rs.35,000 crore in each January, February and March.

The 23rd and final auction week will be held from 1-5 March 2027, with Rs.35,000 crore of 10-year securities scheduled to be issued.

The Centre will issue Rs.15,000 crore of sovereign green bonds in FY27 H2, spread across five auctions of Rs.3,000 crore each. The green bond issuance is included within the Rs.7.86 trillion H2 borrowing programme and does not represent additional borrowing.

The government has retained the option to accept additional subscriptions of up to Rs.2,000 crore against each security through the greenshoe facility.

It will also continue to undertake switches and buybacks of existing government securities to smoothen its redemption profile. Under the announced calendar, switch auctions may be conducted on the third Monday of every month, or more frequently if required.

"The government also retains the flexibility to issue other instruments, including floating-rate bonds and inflation-indexed bonds, depending on its requirements, market conditions and other relevant factors," the finance ministry said.

As per a finance ministry official, net market borrowings (market borrowings for fiscal deficit financing) is kept at the Budget level, implying that in spite of the incipient fiscal pressures the government is committed to the path of fiscal prudence laid out in the Budget.

"The focus on the long end will help us increase our weighted average maturity (WAM), which had fallen during H1. A longer WAM will help reduce the roll-over risk," the official said, declining to be identified.

The government is managing its debt in a prudent manner by resorting to switches and is aiding the market by not adding any additional pressure, the official added.

The Centre's lower borrowing programme could reduce the supply of fresh government securities that the market needs to absorb compared with the original budget plan. However, the impact on bond yields will also depend on inflation, RBI monetary policy, liquidity conditions and investor demand.

Separately, the government plans to borrow Rs.23,000 crore a week through Treasury bills during the third quarter of FY27, covering 13 auction weeks.

The planned weekly issuance comprises Rs.8,000 crore of 91-day T-bills, Rs.8,000 crore of 182-day T-bills and Rs.7,000 crore of 364-day T-bills.

Treasury bills are short-term instruments and are separate from the government's planned Rs.7.86 trillion H2 borrowing through dated securities.

The RBI has also set the government's Ways and Means Advances (WMA) limit at Rs.50,000 crore for H2 FY27. WMA is a temporary source of funds that the government can use to bridge mismatches between its receipts and payments.
